SINGAPORE.name: Singapore
SINGAPORE.keyGuideline: MOH Table of Surgical Procedures (TOSP) & Fee Benchmarks
SINGAPORE.description: Individual responsibility via Medisave accounts and MediShield Life catastrophic coverage. Integrated Shield Plans (IP) with private riders cover private Class A care with mandatory 5% co-pay. MOH Fee Benchmarks strictly scrutinize unindicated revascularization (FFR > 0.80).

UNITED_STATES.name: United States
UNITED_STATES.keyGuideline: ACC/AHA Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC) & Payer Prior Auth
UNITED_STATES.description: High procedural RVU reimbursement under fee-for-service, but insurers aggressively audit and claw back claims lacking pre-authorized clinical indications (Prior Authorization).

UNITED_KINGDOM.name: United Kingdom
UNITED_KINGDOM.description: Universal healthcare free at the point of delivery (0% co-pay). Strict National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) cost-effectiveness thresholds block elective procedures with low QALY gains (< 0.03).

SWEDEN.name: Sweden
SWEDEN.keyGuideline: Swedeheart Quality Registry & Socialstyrelsen National Guidelines
SWEDEN.description: Universal regional county healthcare with annual out-of-pocket maximum caps (Högkostnadsskydd). Real-time nationwide registry tracking (Swedeheart) flags clinical deviations.

JAPAN.name: Japan
JAPAN.keyGuideline: MHLW Medical Fee Schedule (Shinryo Hoshu) & JCS Guidelines
JAPAN.description: Universal coverage with uniform biennial national fee schedule and statutory 30% co-pay, capped on a monthly basis by the High-Cost Medical Expense Benefit (Kogaku Ryoyohi).

SOUTH_KOREA.name: South Korea
SOUTH_KOREA.keyGuideline: HIRA Reimbursement Criteria & Korean Circulation Society Guidelines
SOUTH_KOREA.description: Single-payer national health insurance with advanced diagnostic tech adoption, policed by Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA) automated big data audits and retrospective multi-stent clawbacks.

TAIWAN.name: Taiwan
TAIWAN.keyGuideline: Taiwan NHI Medical Service Payment Standards & Global Budget Cap
TAIWAN.description: Universal smart-card single-payer NHI. Total national expenditures are constrained by a macro Global Budget: when national volume surges exceed spending caps, point reimbursement floats downward (e.g. 0.82 WP/point).

MALAYSIA.name: Malaysia
MALAYSIA.keyGuideline: Ministry of Health Clinical Practice Guidelines & Private Healthcare Act
MALAYSIA.description: Dichotomous system featuring heavily subsidized public hospitals (RM1 outpatient visits) coexisting alongside a rapidly expanding private medical tourism sector billing market fees.

INDONESIA.name: Indonesia
INDONESIA.keyGuideline: BPJS Kesehatan INA-CBG Tariffs & Formularium Nasional (Fornas)
INDONESIA.description: Universal social health insurance (BPJS Kesehatan) under JKN. Reimburses procedures via bundled INA-CBG case-based flat tariffs (e.g. 650 WP ceiling), requiring hospitals to absorb device costs and extra stents.
